The cold baseline gave a strong answer on its own: it refused the naive 'loop against the live number' design, split fast proxies (Lighthouse/a11y/rubric) from the lagging outcome, flagged reward-hacking and dark patterns, and proposed an inner rubric loop + human-gated A/B outer loop. Honest conclusion: the decidability-refusal reasoning is already resident in the base model at this tier, so the decidability gate is a ROBUSTNESS/CONSISTENCY floor (guards regressions and weaker tiers), not measured lift. The skill's measured, discriminating lift is in ROUTING among enumerable / unknown-size / convergence shapes -- eval-3 (saturator vs exhauster) was the strongest discriminator in iteration-1 (5/5 vs 2/5).

Single-sample per configuration (as in iteration-1). The qualitative strength of the baseline answer makes the non-discrimination conclusion solid rather than a sampling artifact, but a multi-sample run would tighten it.
Kept eval-5 in the suite as a documented no-regression floor alongside eval-4, not removed -- it still guards the behavior on weaker models and against future skill edits.
